ports.note: Takes the points to read at and the files a search kept. Emits a long table: one row per point per overpass, and one per point per day with no overpass.

ontology.note: The receipt states the route, the variable, the unit as the file states it, the pixel convention, the quality variable, threshold and operator, files read, points, rows written, and rows passing, below the threshold, with no retrieval and with no overpass; fw:completenessRead true and fw:imputed false. Held by fw:SatellitePointSampleShape.

changes.description: Read, at each point, the value of the swath pixel whose centre is nearest it, in every file Search a satellite catalog kept, by HTTP range in a browser worker, one compressed chunk of latitude and longitude at a time until every point has its pixel, (h5wasm 0.10.3, NIST). Sentinel-5P L2 NO2 on Planetary Computer, with its anonymous token, is the first product with a reader. Each row says whether the value passed qa_value at or above 0.75 (the manual's table) or above it (the readme), compared on the stored integer; where there is no usable value, which gap: no overpass, no retrieval, or below the quality threshold. The value column holds only passing values; value_as_read keeps every value read. Nothing is filled. Experiment 179. The pixel rule is the nearest centre, not the containing pixel the admission review named: the corners cost eight more chunks, roughly doubling a read to 25-30 MB an overpass, and the practitioner chose the nearest centre (experiment 179, 2026-11-05).

evidence.note: Unit tests cover pixel containment, the three gaps, the integer comparison, the table and the receipt. A live browser run read the real files at NYC monitors. No independent recomputation yet: check-coverage is pending.
